nodes.description: Two-dose recombinant subunit vaccine containing varicella-zoster virus glycoprotein E (gE) and the AS01B liposomal adjuvant system (MPL and QS-21). In phase 3 trials, HZ/su achieved 97.2% overall vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster in adults >=50 years of age (ZOE-50) and 91.3% efficacy against herpes zoster plus 88.8% efficacy against postherpetic neuralgia in adults >=70 years of age (pooled ZOE-50/ZOE-70), overcoming the age-related efficacy decline seen with live-attenuated zoster vaccine.
nodes.id: Adjuvanted Recombinant Zoster Vaccine (RZV / Shingrix, VZV gE + AS01B)

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of an adjuvanted herpes zoster subunit vaccine in older adults.
evidence.snippet: During a mean follow-up of 3.2 years, herpes zoster was confirmed in 6 participants in the vaccine group and in 210 participants in the placebo group (incidence rate, 0.3 vs. 9.1 per 1000 person-years) in the modified vaccinated cohort. Overall vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster was 97.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 93.7 to 99.0; P<0.001).

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of the Herpes Zoster Subunit Vaccine in Adults 70 Years of Age or Older.
evidence.snippet: In pooled analyses of data from participants 70 years of age or older in ZOE-50 and ZOE-70 (16,596 participants), vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster was 91.3% (95% CI, 86.8 to 94.5; P<0.001), and vaccine efficacy against postherpetic neuralgia was 88.8% (95% CI, 68.7 to 97.1; P<0.001).

nodes.description: Active VZV replication in sensory ganglia and peripheral nerves provokes hemorrhagic ganglionitis, neuronal injury, and demyelination that manifest acutely as dermatomal vesicular rash and acute herpetic pain, and persist as chronic neuropathic pain (postherpetic neuralgia), cranial nerve palsies, myelitis, meningoencephalitis, or cerebral VZV vasculopathy.

evidence.reference_title: The Spectrum of Neurological Manifestations of Varicella-Zoster Virus Reactivation.
evidence.snippet: While the most frequent reactivation syndrome is herpes zoster, this may be followed by the serious and painful post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN) and by many other neurological conditions. Prominent among these conditions is a VZV vasculopathy, but the role of VZV in causing giant cell arteritis (GCA) is currently controversial. VZV reactivation can also cause segmental motor weakness, myelitis, cranial nerve syndromes, Guillain-Barre syndrome, meningoencephalitis, and zoster sine herpete, where a neurological syndrome occurs in the absence of the zoster rash.

nodes.description: Following primary varicella infection, VZV persists latently in dorsal root, trigeminal, geniculate, and autonomic ganglionic neurons. Immunosenescence or cellular immunosuppression allows latent VZV to reactivate, replicate within ganglionic neurons, and spread anterogradely down sensory axons to the corresponding cutaneous dermatome and central nervous system targets.

evidence.reference_title: The Spectrum of Neurological Manifestations of Varicella-Zoster Virus Reactivation.
evidence.snippet: Varicella-Zoster virus (VZV) is a pathogenic human alpha herpes virus that causes varicella (chicken pox) as a primary infection and, following a variable period of latency in different ganglionic neurons, it reactivates to produce herpes zoster (shingles).

nodes.description: Acute dermatomal neuropathic pain and chronic postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) are the major debilitating manifestations of herpes zoster.

evidence.reference_title: Herpes Zoster Recurrence: A Narrative Review of the Literature.
evidence.snippet: The considerable healthcare burden of HZ is relatively well documented, with approximately one in three individuals experiencing at least one episode during their lifetime, debilitating symptoms including neuropathic pain, and complications such as post-herpetic neuralgia, vision loss, and rarely, stroke, and increased severity in immunocompromised individuals.

nodes.description: Painful unilateral dermatomal vesicular cutaneous eruption is the classic clinical manifestation of herpes zoster.
